rows.question: Why did a fraud model update slow down card authorizations?
rows.answer: The fraud model update (fraud model v4) added new features for card-not-present transactions (roughly 240 features compared to 90 in version 3), which made the fraud-scorer service significantly slower with an observed p99 latency of about 900 ms. Because the payments-gateway calls the fraud-scorer synchronously and keeps the ledger DB connection open until the authorization completes, this increased latency caused ledger database connections to be held much longer. Combined with a recently reduced ledger DB connection pool, this exhaustion of connections caused new authorizations to wait and eventually hit gateway timeouts.

claims.text: Fraud model version 4 added new features for card-not-present transactions, totaling roughly 240 features compared with 90 in version 3.
The update rolled out via CHG-0314 made fraud-scorer much slower, raising observed p99 latency to about 900 ms.
payments-gateway calls fraud-scorer synchronously and keeps the ledger DB connection open until the authorization completes.
Slow fraud scoring kept ledger DB connections checked out much longer than usual, which exhausted the connection pool and led to gateway timeouts.
